title: rotation_curves_chi_field.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: The chi-field modified gravity model must produce galaxy rotation curve fits comparable in quality to standard NFW dark matter halo fits, using the same coupling constant  = 0.01 as in cosmological tests, without additional free parameters.
definitions: chi-field: a modified gravity scalar field that couples to density, with coupling constant .
rotation curve: observed orbital velocity v(r) as a function of radius r for a galaxy.
NFW halo: Navarro-Frenk-White dark matter density profile used as standard model fit.
v_chi(r): predicted rotation velocity from chi-field, computed as sqrt(G_eff(r) * M(r) / r).
: dimensionless coupling constant, set to 0.01 from cosmological constraints.
derivation: For each target galaxy, obtain observational data of velocity vs. radius.
Fit the chi-field modified gravity profile to the rotation data.
Compute chi(r) radial profile using chi-field coupling to density.
Compare chi-field prediction to observation and to standard NFW dark matter halo model.
Assess whether chi-field fits are within observational uncertainty and comparable to NFW fits.
canonical_node.action: Implement and run the chi-field rotation curve fitting procedure for representative galaxies, producing quantitative predictions and comparisons to NFW fits, using  = 0.01 without additional free parameters.
boundary: Does not claim perfect fits; only comparable within observational uncertainty.
Does not establish that chi-field is the correct theory; only that it matches NFW quality.
Does not extend to all galaxies; only representative galaxies from a standard dataset.
Does not provide a full derivation of the chi-field equations; assumes the model is given.
test: For each galaxy, compute chi-field fit and NFW fit; check that chi-field residuals are within observational error bars.
Verify that the same  = 0.01 is used in both galactic and cosmological fits.
Check that no additional free parameters are introduced for the galactic case.
Compare chi-field and NFW fits statistically (e.g., chi-squared) to confirm comparable quality.
